releases.title: More room for your thoughts
notes: Unfinished messages stay intact when a shared link, photo, suggestion or spoken thought arrives. Choose how to use the new content.
Using an earlier request now opens an editable draft. Atlas never sends it again without your tap, and photo requests ask you to reattach the image.
First-time setup puts connecting your PC first, waits for a verified link, and guides you into your first real question. Release notes appear after upgrades.
Connection status distinguishes a saved desktop, an active attempt, a user disconnect and a failed link.
Chat gives the conversation more room with a smaller header, Atlas rail and empty state.
Voice controls announce Stop reading or Stop dictation when active. Android settings are available after microphone permission is denied.

releases.title: A companion you can count on
notes: Your unfinished messages and attached photos are saved privately in each phone conversation, including while offline. Nothing is sent automatically.
Find, rename, archive, copy or delete phone conversations. Older local transcripts that fell out of the chat list are recovered where available.
Connection drops now end the interrupted reply cleanly. Reconnecting does not replay your request.
Talk to Atlas from Quick Settings waits for the connection to be ready. On-device dictation can save a draft while offline.
Live talk handles Stop more reliably when Atlas mentions the word in a longer reply. Approval prompts are easier to reach with accessibility tools.
A downloaded update stays available to review and install when your desktop or GitHub is temporarily unreachable.
Connection diagnostics explain the stage that failed without including your messages, addresses or pairing credentials.
Connect on open now follows your preference and foreground state more consistently.
Desktop companion changes add individual phone revocation, conversation management and memory correction. These require the updated desktop code and a restart.

releases.title: Atlas at your fingertips
notes: Share a screenshot or photo from another Android app into an editable Atlas request. Atlas re-encodes it without source metadata and waits for you to press Send.
The Atlas Live home-screen widget shows real connection and work state without displaying chat text or private paths.
A Quick Settings tile opens the phone's Live talk surface with one deliberate tap. Permission and foreground rules still apply.

releases.title: Room to breathe
notes: The chat now gives conversations the space they deserve, with a compact Atlas presence that stays alive without covering your messages.
A fixed wordmark, quieter navigation, simpler composer and smaller voice controls make the phone feel calm and deliberate.
Long replies and code are easier to read. The layout has been checked on compact screens and at larger text sizes.

releases.title: A quicker way home
notes: When home Wi-Fi is unreachable, Atlas switches to the verified private 5G route faster.
The GitHub update flow was installed and verified on a phone over 5G, including the post-install journal.

releases.title: Atlas travels with you
notes: The updater can find releases on GitHub even when the paired desktop is out of reach.
Downloads are checked for package, version, size, SHA-256 and the installed signing certificate before Android offers installation.
A verified Tailscale route lets the same desktop Companion answer your phone away from home.

releases.title: An unrecorded step
notes: No separate 0.10.0 Android release notes were preserved. The documented history resumes at 0.10.1.

releases.title: Conversations with continuity
notes: Phone chats gained their own encrypted conversation list, separate from desktop chats.
Atlas can retrieve relevant context from the 10 most recent phone chats without mixing them into desktop history.
Phone requests stay visible in the desktop Companion while their conversations remain separate.

releases.title: His real voice
notes: Live talk and Read use the voice selected in desktop Companion instead of the phone's generic system voice.
Voice travels over the existing authenticated, certificate-pinned connection and stops when you interrupt or leave Chat.

releases.title: One Atlas, two screens
notes: A live pairing QR links the phone to the normal desktop Companion.
Build progress, saved results and requested previews follow real work on the PC.
Live talk, optional reconnect, private Signals and explicit connection status made the companion more present.

releases.title: Keep what you make
notes: An encrypted mission library saves build receipts, step timelines and isolated website previews on the phone.
Interrupted work is labeled honestly. Refinement prepares a new draft, while Forget removes only the phone receipt.

releases.title: The droid comes alive
notes: New shared sprite animations let the original Atlas greet, listen, think, speak, code, review and rest on both devices.
Phone requests summon the existing desktop Companion and show their real work there.

releases.title: More than a chat
notes: You could attach a photo, follow phone-origin build milestones and preview a generated website.
Encrypted memory cards became separate from chat, with explicit save, edit and delete controls.
On-device dictation and private VPN pairing laid the foundation for using Atlas away from home.

releases.title: A companion takes shape
notes: The original droid gained a warm native stage, custom type, amber light and a more expressive phone interface.
Chat, navigation, composer, connection and update journal were redesigned with accessible motion controls.
